0x61b2760.name: rocksdb::Tracer::IteratorSeekForPrev
quirks: On the skip path IteratorSeekForPrev returns Status::OK() without consulting the clock: a flagged or oversized seek leaves the clock's call count at 0 and the sampling counter untouched (flag skips) -- the gate runs before the timestamp is read.

The type byte lives in its own stack slot (rsp+0x23) passed by address to ShouldSkipTrace, then copied into trace.type at rsp+0x38 after the gate passes; ShouldSkipTrace reads the type through that pointer (movzbl 0x0(%rbp) at 0x61b1949).

The varint length prefix encodes the LOW 32 bits of each slice size (key: mov 0x8(%r13),%esi at 0x61b2a08; lower: the size passes through rsi/esi at 0x61b2a6d; upper: mov r15d,%esi at 0x61b2a84) while the append copies the full size_t -- a >4 GiB slice would prefix the truncated length; untestable at that scale, recorded from the disassembly.

The payload_map bits are never serialized by EncodeTrace; they are visible only as the first 8 payload bytes (PutFixed64). The map is 48 with empty bounds, 112 with lower only, 176 with upper only, 240 with both.

The timestamp comes from the 13-layer SystemClockWrapper::NowMicros fast path (each layer's vtable slot 19 compared against 0x5d4d490, followed through +0x20); the first layer whose slot differs calls that slot's function directly instead of continuing the chain.

The CF id is the uint32_t the caller passes by reference (loaded with a 32-bit load at 0x61b29d2) and stored little-endian as 4 bytes; it is NOT varint-encoded. (Unlike Get, there is no ColumnFamilyHandle vtable call here -- the caller already resolved the id.)

The upper bound arrives by value: the caller copies its two words onto the stack (movdqu/movups at the call site 0x5d55597-0x5d555ad); the function keeps the data pointer at [rsp+0x10] and the size in r15.

The exception landing pad at 0x61b2c9c..0x61b2ca7 (endbr64; mov rbx,rax; jmp 0x61b2738) runs only on the exception path (bad_alloc from the string appends); the string length guards raise length_error instead (std::string::_M_append, via __throw_length_error).

The payload string is freed only when its pointer differs from the SSO buffer at rsp+0x58 (standard string destruction); the three 5-byte varint buffers sit at rsp+0x69 (key), rsp+0x6e (lower) and rsp+0x73 (upper), just below the stack canary at rsp+0x78.
rules: if ShouldSkipTrace(this, type) (0x61b1930) returns true, return Status::OK() at once (no clock call, no writer call)
